This is one of the first species that caught my eye. As thorny as it is beautiful, I think it has to be one of the most impressive bromeliads out there. It's tenacious too, starting in South and Central America, and reaching all the way up into Floriday. It's not picky about soil and can tolerate being beaten by the sun all day. Here's a few interesting facts I found:

  • Used as natural "fencing" for livestock
  • Colloquially referred to as 'Heart of flame' and wild pineapple
  • Contains an edible fruit which is cleaned and peeled like a banana
  • "Medicinally the juice of the fruit has been employed for many uses from treating intestinal parasites, fevers, oral ulcers and to induce abortions."
